source_name: Alza.cz newsroom – Adyen partnership announcement
why_relevant: Primary confirmation that the largest Czech e-tailer switched its online AND in-store terminal acquiring to Adyen, unifying providers across all countries it operates in. This is exactly the buy-side switch signal the cell targets, and implies displacement of an incumbent CZ acquirer.

source_name: Merchant checkout / payment-options help pages (Alza, Rohlík, Notino, Košík)
why_relevant: Public 'možnosti platby' pages enumerate accepted methods and frequently name the gateway/bank buttons (Platba 24, eKonto Online, MojePlatba, Apple/Google Pay, BNPL partners). Diffed over time they reveal PSP switches before any press release. Alza's corporate-card surcharge page also shows merchant reaction to interchange/commercial-card fees.

source_name: Cvak A2A payment rollout coverage (Albert, Lidl) – Měšec.cz / HN / Deník
why_relevant: Highest-value current buy-side signal: major grocery chains (Albert first, then Lidl CZ across ~326 stores) adopting Cvak account-to-account payments — backed notably by Air Bank, with Fio, mBank and Moneta clients supported — explicitly to cut card-scheme fees and as a fallback during card outages. Direct evidence of card-rail disintermediation driven by merchant economics.

source_name: Měšec.cz – consumer finance/payments daily
why_relevant: Long-running CZ personal-finance outlet that reports payment method launches, fee changes, bank outages and consumer disputes earlier and more technically than mainstream media; strong snowball hub to merchants, banks and PSPs.

source_name: Peníze.cz – bank outage and payments reporting
why_relevant: Documents multi-bank electronic banking/payment outages (e.g. simultaneous Air Bank, Fio, ČS, KB, ČSOB disruption attributed to DDoS) — outage chronology is a core demand-side reliability signal for this cell and a substitute for a CZ-specific Downdetector archive.

source_name: dTest – Spotřebitelská poradna a články o platbách
why_relevant: Largest CZ consumer organisation; its advice board and articles ('Co dělat, když se mýlí banka', card-surcharge/SCA explainers) surface recurring consumer failure modes with banks, card payments and gateways, and it operates the complaint mediation portal.

source_name: VašeStížnosti.cz (dTest ADR complaint portal)
why_relevant: Public, per-merchant complaint database operated by dTest. Contains named complaints such as 'Nefunkční platební brána a mnohonásobné stržení částky z účtu' — i.e. concrete failing gateway implementations, duplicate captures, refund failures, per merchant, with merchant responses. Unmatched granularity for demand-side failure signals.

source_name: Česká národní banka – Ochrana spotřebitele / podání a dohledová statistika
why_relevant: CNB receives and investigates consumer submissions about payment institutions and publishes supervisory statistics; also transposes EBA guidelines on PSD2 complaint handling. Aggregate complaint volumes per supervised entity are a regulator-grade demand-side quality signal.

source_name: Portál gov.cz – rozcestník stížností na finanční instituce
why_relevant: Official signpost mapping which complaint body handles which payment dispute type (ČNB vs finanční arbitr vs ČOI); useful to enumerate the full CZ complaint-channel landscape for this cell.

source_name: APEK – Asociace pro elektronickou komerci (E-commerce Study, payment method surveys)
why_relevant: The CZ e-commerce trade association publishes recurring studies quantifying payment-method mix at checkout (card-in-advance vs dobírka vs bank buttons vs BNPL) — the canonical demand-side adoption dataset, with a time series back to at least 2014 and a 2025 edition.

source_name: Dopravní podnik hl. m. Prahy – bezkontaktní platba jízdného / samoobslužná odbavovací zařízení
why_relevant: Prague transit operator documents its open-loop contactless fare payment estate (roughly 800 tram terminals, 90 metro-station devices, ~1200 added on buses). Transit ticketing is a flagship buy-side payment deployment; the operator pages plus PID announcements track rollout scale and phases.

source_name: PID / Pražská integrovaná doprava – news portal (pid.cz)
why_relevant: Integrated-transport authority news announces ticketing/payment technology milestones across operators and the PID Lítačka app; pointer to further operators, card issuers (XT-Card) and the DOS clearing system ecosystem.

source_name: České dráhy – onboard card acceptance / self-service rail terminals (with ČSOB)
why_relevant: National rail operator equipped 1600+ conductors with mobile terminals in cooperation with ČSOB, and publishes user manuals for self-service rail terminals. A rare named merchant-acquirer relationship in the transport vertical, plus regional IDS deployments (IDSOK/KIDSOK contactless check-in).

source_name: Přepravní a tarifní věstník (MD ČR) – carrier tariffs and transport conditions
why_relevant: Official bulletin publishing carrier tariffs and transport conditions (e.g. RegioJet) which specify accepted payment methods, surcharges and refund mechanics — an authoritative, archived record of payment acceptance rules in transport.

source_name: Lidl ČR – zákaznické informace: platby na samoobslužné pokladně
why_relevant: Retailer's own help centre stating which payment methods are accepted at self-checkout — first-party confirmation of in-store acceptance changes (cards, wallets, Cvak) as SCO estates expand across 320+ stores.

source_name: Toret.net / WPify / platiti.cz – third-party CZ payment plugin vendors for WooCommerce & PrestaShop
why_relevant: Independent plugin houses publish changelogs listing exactly which CZ/SK gateways they support and when new gateway APIs, Apple Pay, deferred payment or Besteron/ThePay/Comgate versions land. Changelogs are a high-frequency, machine-readable leading indicator of gateway feature rollout and merchant demand.

source_name: WordPress.org plugin directory – Czech payment gateway plugins (active installs, support forums)
why_relevant: Provides quantitative adoption proxies (active install counts, version cadence, last-updated) for CZ gateway plugins and a public support forum where merchants report integration failures — both an adoption metric and a complaint channel.

source_name: Adyen Knowledge Hub – Czech merchant case studies (Alza)
why_relevant: Supplier-published but merchant-validated case study describing why a major Czech merchant consolidated online + POS acquiring; template for finding equivalent case studies from other PSPs (Comgate, GoPay, Global Payments, Worldline, Nexi) targeting CZ merchants.

source_name: Rohlik Group Tech Blog
why_relevant: Engineering blog of a major CZ-origin online grocer that operates checkout across several markets; engineering posts and the group's online-services/cookie policy disclose payment processors in use (Adyen among them) and architecture choices behind checkout.

source_name: Global Payments CZ – doplněk pro Shoptet (GP webpay merchant integration page)
why_relevant: Shows an incumbent CZ acquirer defending the SMB e-commerce channel via platform plugins; comparing such pages across acquirers reveals where each is fighting for merchant share and which platforms they prioritise.

source_name: aRecenze.cz – consumer-facing bank/payment incident and review coverage
why_relevant: Aggregates consumer-perspective reporting on bank app outages, retailer payment launches (Cvak at Lidl, naming supported banks) and self-checkout changes; fast-moving demand-side sentiment layer that often surfaces incidents before official confirmation.

source_name: ČNB – Seznamy regulovaných a registrovaných subjektů (JERRS)
why_relevant: The single canonical application enumerating every licensed/registered financial market entity in CZ: banks, payment institutions (platební instituce), e-money institutions, small-scale payment service providers (PPSMR), small-scale e-money issuers, plus PSD2 notifications from foreign TPPs. This is the definitive competitor/actor universe for CZ payments — including fintechs that never appear in media — and each entry is a launch point for vendor, partner and case-study research.

source_name: ČNB – Seznamy a evidence (supervision lists hub)
why_relevant: Hub page that enumerates every list ČNB publishes (JERRS, WS JERRS, open data, prospectus registers, rating agencies, other lists). Best single entry point for snowballing to all regulator-maintained pointer sources; an EN mirror exists at /en/supervision-financial-market/lists-registers/.

source_name: ČNB – Otevřená data (open data datasets of regulated entities)
why_relevant: Machine-readable CSV+JSON-schema exports of ČNB registers published under Government Regulation 425/2016 Sb. Confirmed datasets include banks and foreign bank branches, money changers (směnárny), non-bank consumer credit providers and credit intermediaries, addressed via numbered endpoints (JERRS.OPENDATA.STAHUJ?p_seznam=N). This is the lowest-friction, highest-fidelity way to maintain a live CZ actor list with IČO keys.

source_name: ČNB – Webové služby WS JERRS (register web services API)
why_relevant: Official API over the register, live since 1 July 2019 — the structured, queryable route to entity data (licences, scopes of permitted payment services, changes over time). Important caveat for planning: authentication requires a commercial certificate (eIdentity, I.CA, PostSignum or an EU trust-list CA), so it is not anonymously accessible.

source_name: ČNB – Platební instituce a instituce elektronických peněz (legislative/regulatory base)
why_relevant: Defines the CZ licence taxonomy (PI, IEP, PPSMR, VEPMR) that any competitor-set model must mirror, and links out to the corresponding registers and rules. Essential for correctly bucketing register entries into payments market segments.

source_name: ČNB – Licencování a povolovací řízení: poskytovatelé platebních služeb a vydavatelé elektronických peněz
why_relevant: Documents how entities enter the register — the licensing pipeline. Useful for anticipating new market entrants and for understanding what documentation (business plan, outsourcing, ICT arrangements) applicants must submit, which indirectly reveals vendor dependencies.

source_name: ČNB – Pravomocná rozhodnutí (final enforcement decisions, proceedings opened after 1.1.2009)
why_relevant: Full-text sanction and remedial-measure decisions naming specific banks, payment institutions and small-scale providers. These documents frequently describe operational detail — systems, outsourcing arrangements, AML/transaction-monitoring tooling, failures of specific processes — which is otherwise unobtainable vendor/competitor intelligence. Also the earliest public signal of a distressed or exiting competitor.
